topic: SP-070 security review lows and accepted limits
detail: From four security-audit rounds on PR #167 (all critical/high/medium fixed): (1) operator-only rests on refuseNonOperator, so a process an agent detaches from its session (reparented to launchd) passes as the operator, as for ApplySpaces; (2) a process running as the user can write spaces_enforcement and its log consistently while orchd is stopped, which the next start takes (the switch still shows in every digest and status); (3) a project-level Claude Code 'disableAllHooks' turns off every hook including the digest, outside any switch; (4) when orchd does not answer, the digest's fallback reads orch.db's switches but not whether the tool hooks are still in settings.json; (5) with every orch hook gone from Claude Code's settings no digest runs and the hooks layer reads as enforcing (orch status lists the tool hooks as missing); (6) markGuardState labels an event with the guard state when orchd stores it, a few milliseconds after the hook ran, and the log's writer waits on the switches' lock while a switch writes settings.json; (7) GetEnforcement is open to every caller and checks Claude Code's settings at most every 5 s; (8) settings.Service.List ignores a sync error except through the provider state, which the hooks check now reads. Self-protection paths (SP-042) and the OS sandbox (SP-046) are the answers to (1)-(3).
